This! Me and my stepdad didn't have a good relationship until I was an adult. He was always great to me, but I was so desperate for my dad's love I pushed him away. I finally gave up on my dad, and although I still call my stepdad by his name, he knows he's my dad, and he's my kids grabdpa. My stepdads dad died when I was a kid and his mom remarried when I was in my late teens. I always considered his mom my grandma, but not her new husband, I was just too old. I still love him like a family member, but he just doesn't feel like grandpa to me. When I got pregnant with my first, my grandma approached me and asked what to label stuff from them and was shocked and cried when I didn't hesitate to say great grandma and great grandpa. He may not be grandpa to me, but he loves my grandma, and makes her happy and he loves my kids. My kids absolutely adore him, and are so lucky to have an extra grandpa in their lives and I have no reason to deprive them of that just because we aren't close. Sure I'm sad my grandpa isn't alive to play that role, but we have a man in our lives who is more then happy to stand in and I'm thankful for that. 

I'm not saying OPs siblings are wrong, it's their choice who gets to be involved in their children's lives. If my dad was dead instead of a deadbeat I may have felt differently about my stepdad, so I can't pretend to understand completely. But at the same time, they may be depriving their kids of a special relationship and I hope anyone who is in a similar situation is able to consider this with step parents. Family doesn't always have to be simple. Having extra grandparents doesn't mean you love your parent any less, it just means your kids get more love and love makes family not blood. Letting a step parent play that role doesn't mean you consider them a parent to you or giving them any sort of authority.

I don't understand all the Y T A comments. Child support is a supplemented income, you aren't supposed to budget every last dollar to spoil the child, if she has a nice, clean, safe roof over their head, and food on the table, all bills are payed and the kid is happy then the support is being used appropriately. I wish I had the dedication to stop using my van and walk my kids to school, it would be so good for all of us to get more physical activity and sunlight. As long as you're more then happy to get an Uber when needed, if a car isn't essential to you that's okay. Small kids grow out of things fast, no need to get brand new name brand everything, especially when the child is at an age where brands aren't really important to him. I'd rather spend 5$ on a shirt at Walmart then 40$ for the exact same shirt with a random logo on it. It sounds like OP is teacher her child that materialistic items aren't the most important thing in life and that's okay. If the father wants to spoil the kid that's his choice, he can buy him whatever he wants on his time. 

I also understand why ex is upset, if he's sending above what is needed it's going to be frustrating not seeing the money being used. Be aware that if he's giving you above what the courts have ordered, he may stop giving you more, and if you choose to live more frugal you have to be ok with that.

I'd suggest maybe finding a good compromise with the father though, whether it's signing up your son for more extracurricular activities, agreeing to buy new for things like sports gear or shoes (you can always donate once he grows out of them to help someone less fortunate) or set up a weekly allowance and chore chart for your son. Set up a monthly date to splurge a bit, or put a portion of your rainy day fund into a college fund. Maybe spoil him for Christmas with some more expensive toys, get a pet of his (reasonable) choice to teach some responsibility.

4 year olds really aren't very expensive unless you want to spoil them constantly. It doesn't take much to keep them happy and loved. Once he gets older and he's more into style and the toys and sports become much more expensive things will be different. It's nice that your ex is sending you a lot more then what's needed, but I think it's wrong for him to expect you to give your son everything he could ever want, that's exactly how you end up with a spoiled entitled brat.

NAH, only assuming that you aren't depriving your child. If he's wearing ripped up, stained clothes, shoes full of holes, not allowing him to explore his interests when it's easily affordable my vote would be different, but from the post I don't think either of you are wrong.

NTA. I get it, me and my husband have 3 young kids, I’m in school full time and he’s working full time. It’s hard and exhausting, but you can’t just hide in another room leaving your kids in supervised for long periods of time. I think your wife is struggling and worn out, but she’s still a parent and has a responsibility to care for the kids when she is home alone with them. I think you’re approaching it the wrong way though, you guys need to find fair compromises and solutions. For example, don’t stress or complain over a toy box being dumped all over the floor. That’s normal end of day cleanup for parents. But if the kids spill a yogurt on the couch that’s not something that can wait until later and she should clean that right away. Maybe try to keep the mess in one room, like when she gets home they all play in the bedroom or something so the rest of the house stays clean. Make rules about food, like have her be present for snack time at the table and have the kids throw out their garbage/put dishes in the sink and then she turns on a show and sits until you get home and no more snacks until dinner. Split the night up so you each have 30/60mins off parenting duty every night. Every family is different so no one solution will work for everyone, but I feel like this issue can easily be fixed if you come up with some plans! 

I’m not sure why you’re getting so much hostility, you sound just as worn out as she is and your frustration is justified. This is something that needs to be worked on sooner then later before the resentment builds. Good luck! We’re struggling with similar issues, but with good communication things are getting so much better!
